README: THE LISTING-GRAPHIC SPECIFICATION, ONE ROW PER ASSET, EVERY NUMBER WITH THE URL IT WAS READ FROM AND THE DATE IT WAS READ.

It belongs to the TOOLCHAIN and not to any tool, for the reason check-store-metadata.mjs already states about scripts/schema/tool.schema.json: the store vocabulary is the vocabulary of the stores, and resolving it against the tree being graded would let a fixture supply its own idea of what a store requires. `check-listing-assets.mjs` grades a tool against this file; `render-extension-graphics.mjs` renders the tool's assets FROM this file. One declaration, two readers -- the renderer cannot produce a size the guard does not expect, and the guard cannot demand a size the renderer does not know how to make.

A LIMIT WITH NO `source` IS REFUSED, NOT ENFORCED. Same rule as tool.json storeMetadata, same reason: an invented limit fires on CORRECT input. check-listing-assets.mjs fails on any row whose `source` is not an https URL or whose `fetched` is not a date, BEFORE it looks at a single pixel.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. No maximum FILE SIZE for any of the three extension stores: developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/images, learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-edge/extensions/publish/publish-extension and extensionworkshop.com's listing page were all fetched on 2026-09-20 and none of them states one. The only image-adjacent size limit found anywhere on AMO is the 200 MB add-on PACKAGE limit, which is about the .xpi and not about a picture. A byte ceiling is therefore not written here and not enforced.

No SCREENSHOT COLOUR TYPE either. Chrome's page states 'Square corners, no padding (full bleed)' and gives the two accepted pixel sizes; it does NOT state a bit depth or an alpha rule for screenshots, and neither does Edge's or AMO's. The extension tree's own screenshots/README.md used to assert '24-bit PNG, no alpha' with no URL beside it -- correct-sounding, unsourceable, and exactly the shape this file exists to stop. The icon's transparency IS sourced, and is enforced; the screenshots' is not, and is not.

screenshots._dirWhy: ONE capture set, in the shared directory, because 1280x800 is the only size all three stores accept -- so three copies would be three chances to update two of them. tool.json storeMetadata.sharedDir names where that directory lives; this key names its name inside it.

effective._why: DERIVED FROM THE THREE `perStore` BLOCKS BELOW, and the derivation is stated rather than left to a reader: sizes is their INTERSECTION (Chrome takes 1280x800 or 640x400, Edge takes 1280x800 or 640x480, AMO recommends 1280x800 -- one size is common to all three); min is the largest of the required minimums (Chrome 1, the only store that requires any); max is the smallest of the stated maximums (Chrome 5, against Edge 6 and AMO's 'no practical limit'). check-listing-assets.mjs recomputes this from perStore and FAILS if this block disagrees with it -- two declarations of one fact, held to each other rather than trusted.

chrome.verbatim: at least 1-and preferably the maximum allowed 5-screenshots | 1280x800 or 640x400 pixels | Square corners, no padding (full bleed)

edge.verbatim: Screenshots | Optional | You can submit a maximum of 6 screenshots describing the functionality of the extension in detail. The size of the screenshots must be either 640 x 480 pixels or 1280 x 800 pixels.
edge._note: EDGE'S SMALL SIZE IS 640x480 AND CHROME'S IS 640x400. One digit apart, in adjacent cells, and the reason only 1280x800 is captured.

firefox.verbatim: capture images that are 1280x800px (the maximum image display size) | There isn't a practical limit to the number of screenshots you can include
firefox._note: AMO documents a RECOMMENDATION, not a requirement: no page fetched on 2026-09-20 says a listing is refused without a screenshot. `required: false` records that, and it is why the effective minimum comes from Chrome alone.

assets._colorTypeWhy: COLOUR TYPE 6 IS THE SOURCED REQUIREMENT AND NOT A PREFERENCE. Chrome asks for the artwork to occupy 96x96 with 'an additional 16 pixels per side ... transparent padding'; padding that is transparent cannot exist in colour type 2. artworkBox below is that 96, and the renderer centres the mark in it.
assets.verbatim: 128x128-pixel extension icon image | The actual icon size should be 96x96 (for square icons); an additional 16 pixels per side should be transparent padding | The image must be in PNG format
assets._firefoxWhy: AMO IS RECOMMENDED, NOT REQUIRED, AND ITS TWO CURRENT PAGES DISAGREE ABOUT THE NUMBER. extensionworkshop.com's listing guidance (fetched 2026-09-20) says 'You can load icons at two resolutions-32x32 and 64x64-in either PNG or JPEG format'; mozilla.github.io/addons-server's API reference recommends a 128x128 upload that AMO resizes itself. A 128x128 upload satisfies both readings, so the file Chrome requires is the file AMO gets, and no second slot is created for a number two pages cannot agree on.

assets._colorTypeWhy: NO ALPHA RULE IS STATED FOR THIS ASSET ANYWHERE ON THE PAGE, so none is invented: both 8-bit colour types are accepted here and the renderer picks 2 because the tile is a filled rectangle with nothing behind it. Chrome's page lists PNG and JPEG as the accepted formats for a promotional image; this factory emits PNG because every other asset it emits is PNG.
assets._why: THIS IS THE ASSET THAT MAKES CAPTURING SCREENSHOTS INSUFFICIENT. A Chrome Web Store submission without it is refused at upload, and until 2026-09-20 no slot for it existed anywhere in the extension tree -- so a lane that captured five perfect screenshots would have bought a listing that still could not be submitted.

assets.verbatim: Extension logo | Required for each language | An image (one per language) that represents your company or extension logo, with an aspect ratio of 1:1 and a recommended size of 300 x 300 pixels, with a minimum size of 128 x 128 pixels.
assets._perLanguageWhy: 'REQUIRED FOR EACH LANGUAGE' IS A DASHBOARD FACT, NOT A FILE FACT. The same page's Step 7 says the logo is copied across languages from Partner Center itself -- 'click the Duplicate option ... For example, click Duplicate this logo for all languages'. One file in the tree therefore serves every language the package declares, and the per-language duty is discharged by one click in the dashboard rather than by N identical PNGs in git. Recorded here so nobody adds _locales-shaped copies later.
assets._minimumWhy: The page states a MINIMUM of 128x128 and a RECOMMENDED 300x300. The recommended size is what is rendered and what is enforced: a guard that accepted anything at or above the minimum would pass a 128x128 logo that Edge would then upscale, which is a quality loss nothing downstream could see.

unverified: CHROME MARQUEE PROMOTIONAL TILE (1400x560) -- optional on the page fetched 2026-09-20 ('You can provide one of each of the following'), so no slot is created and none is required. Without it the extension cannot be featured in the marquee, which is a discovery consequence and not a submission blocker.

EDGE SMALL (440x280) AND LARGE (1400x560) PROMOTIONAL TILES -- both stated Optional on the same page. The 440x280 file Chrome requires would satisfy Edge's optional small tile byte-for-byte; it is not declared for Edge because declaring an optional asset as required is how a guard starts failing on correct input.
SCREENSHOT MAXIMUM FILE SIZE, ALL THREE STORES -- not documented on any page fetched 2026-09-20. Not written, not enforced.
SCREENSHOT COLOUR TYPE / BIT DEPTH, ALL THREE STORES -- not documented. The tree's previous '24-bit PNG, no alpha' line carried no URL and is not reproduced here.
